ideas.name: SonicLens
ideas.niche: Mobile-based acoustic diagnostic and DIY soundproofing guidance.
ideas.problem: The high cost and technical complexity of professional acoustic engineering, making it difficult for non-experts to identify specific frequency leaks or echo patterns in non-studio environments.
ideas.targetUser: Remote professionals, aspiring podcasters, and bedroom musicians (ages 20-40) working in untreated residential spaces like spare bedrooms or living rooms.
coreFeatures: Real-time Frequency Spectrogram Visualization
Spatial Sound Leak Mapping (Walk-the-Room Mode)
Acoustic Profile Report Generation
Personalized DIY Treatment Roadmap & Shopping List
realDependencies: High-fidelity FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) audio processing library
TensorFlow Lite or CoreML for acoustic pattern recognition
ARKit/ARCore for spatial room mapping and heat-map overlay
Affiliate Product API (e.g., Amazon) for acoustic material recommendations
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will bypass real-time audio math by playing a curated .wav file containing embedded 'problem frequencies' (e.g., a 300Hz hum). A mock FFT service will feed the UI a JSON array of frequency magnitudes that are hardcoded to oscillate in sync with the audio. Spatial scanning will be simulated by using the device's accelerometer to move a 'hotspot' icon across a static 2D room image; if the user tilts the phone toward a 'leak' coordinate, a detection event is triggered. The recommendation engine will return a deterministic response based on which 'leak' frequency was detected in the mock audio loop.

ideas.name: SolSync
ideas.niche: Circadian rhythm optimization through real-time environmental light scheduling
ideas.problem: Difficulty regulating sleep-wake cycles, cortisol levels, and mood due to inconsistent exposure to natural light windows, exacerbated by indoor-centric lifestyles and unpredictable weather.
ideas.targetUser: Remote-working professionals (25-45), biohackers, and individuals managing seasonal affective disorder (SAD) who require precise, data-driven cues to optimize their biological clock.
coreFeatures: Dynamic Sunlight Windows: Real-time push notifications identifying the 'Golden Window' for morning light exposure based on local solar altitude and UV index.
Chronotype Calibration: Personalized scheduling algorithms that adjust alert times based on the user's specific biological chronotype (e.g., Lion, Bear, Wolf).
Weather-Adaptive Rescheduling: Intelligent rescheduling that detects high cloud cover or precipitation and suggests alternative windows or supplemental light therapy.
Bio-Correlation Dashboard: A visual interface that overlays sunlight exposure logs against sleep quality and energy metrics from wearable devices.
realDependencies: Geolocation API (Google Maps Platform or CoreLocation)
Weather API (OpenWeatherMap or Apple WeatherKit for cloud cover/UV data)
Solar Position API (SunCalc or specialized astronomical data services)
Health Data APIs (Apple HealthKit or Google Fit for biometric correlation)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a 'MockEnvironmentEngine' that intercepts all asynchronous service calls. Geolocation will be hardcoded to a specific latitude/longitude (e.g., San Francisco) with a 'Simulate Transit' toggle that increments coordinates every 5 seconds. Weather and solar data will be served from a local JSON manifest containing a pre-scripted 48-hour weather cycle (alternating between 'Clear', 'Partly Cloudy', and 'Overcast'). Every API request will be wrapped in a Promise that introduces a randomized delay of 800ms to 2500ms to trigger and demonstrate loading states. Biometric data (sleep scores/HRV) will be generated using a pseudo-random walk algorithm to ensure data looks realistic and continuous rather than purely erratic.

ideas.name: PlateSense
ideas.problem: The cognitive gap between abstract nutritional data (grams/calories) and physical reality, which leads to frequent calorie underestimation and friction-heavy manual logging.
ideas.targetUser: Health-conscious adults (25-45) and individuals managing metabolic conditions like diabetes or obesity who require high-precision macronutrient tracking without the manual effort of weighing food.
coreFeatures: Volumetric AR Overlay: Real-time 3D estimation of food volume mapped directly onto the user's plate using spatial tracking.
Macro-Heatmaps: Color-coded AR layers (e.g., Blue for Protein, Yellow for Carbs) that visually segment a single food item by its nutritional composition.
Ghost-Portion Guide: A translucent 'ideal portion' overlay that shows the user how their current serving compares to their personalized nutritional goals.
Instant Macro-Log: A single-tap feature that converts visual volume data into a digital log entry for seamless syncing with health ecosystems.
realDependencies: ARKit (iOS) or ARCore (Android) for spatial mapping and plane detection
LiDAR API for high-precision depth sensing and volumetric calculation
Computer Vision model (TensorFlow Lite/CoreML) for food type segmentation
Nutritionix or Edamam API for real-time macronutrient data retrieval
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a 'Simulated Scan' workflow. Instead of live camera processing, the app will present a gallery of 5 pre-set 'Target Plates'. When a user selects a plate, the app will trigger a 2-second 'Analyzing...' loading animation with a simulated progress bar. The 'AR' overlays will be implemented as 2D SVG graphics anchored to fixed coordinate points on the image to mimic a 3D depth effect. All nutritional data will be pulled from a local JSON mock file containing hardcoded results for the 5 pre-set plates, with a forced 1000ms delay to simulate real-world API network latency.

ideas.name: UnLoop
ideas.niche: Subscription-cancellation path finding and dark pattern navigation
ideas.problem: The 'subscription trap' where companies use intentional UI complexity, hidden buttons, and circular confirmation loops (dark patterns) to prevent users from cancelling services.
ideas.targetUser: Digital-native adults aged 18-45, particularly budget-conscious students and subscription-heavy professionals, who are frustrated by 'hidden' cancellation flows and unintended recurring charges.
coreFeatures: Interactive Step-by-Step Visual Walkthroughs
Dark Pattern Warning Alerts (e.g., 'Warning: This button actually re-subscribes you')
Direct-to-Billing Deep Link Vault
Community-Sourced Path Updates
Cancellation Progress Checklist
realDependencies: Cloud-based Content Management System (CMS) for visual assets
Deep-linking/URL Scheme handling service
Real-time crowdsourced data API
Global Search API (e.g., Algolia) for service lookup
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will implement a local 'MockServer' module that intercepts all fetch requests. It will serve a hardcoded JSON payload containing a library of 20+ services, each with nested 'step' objects (containing mock image URLs, instruction text, and 'danger_level' flags). To simulate real-world API behavior, a 'NetworkSimulator' utility will apply randomized delays between 400ms and 1500ms to every request. Deep links will be emulated by opening a controlled internal WebView that loads pre-rendered HTML 'mock-sites' instead of actual external URLs. Community updates will be simulated by a 'DataInjector' that populates the UI with fake 'Recently Verified' timestamps and user-generated comments.

ideas.name: SeatSpy
ideas.problem: The uncertainty and discomfort of commuting in overcrowded or unexpectedly packed train carriages during rush hour, leading to wasted time and physical fatigue.
ideas.targetUser: Daily metropolitan commuters, students, and office workers (ages 18-45) who rely on heavy rail transit and value seat availability for comfort, work, or privacy.
coreFeatures: Live Carriage Heatmap: A visual, color-coded schematic of the incoming train showing real-time density per car (Green/Yellow/Red).
One-Tap Reporting: A high-speed UI allowing users to report 'Empty', 'Few Seats', 'Standing Room Only', or 'Packed' with a single tap.
Smart Arrival Alerts: Proximity-based push notifications that warn users when a high-density train is approaching their station.
Commuter Karma: A gamified reputation system that awards points and badges to users who provide frequent and accurate occupancy reports.
realDependencies: GTFS-Realtime API for live train positions and schedule data
Mapbox or Google Maps API for station-based spatial visualization
Firebase Realtime Database for instantaneous crowdsourced data synchronization
Geofencing API for location-triggered notifications
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will implement a 'Virtual Transit Engine'—a local JavaScript service that replaces real APIs. Instead of GTFS, it will serve a static JSON object containing 3 simulated subway lines, each with 8 cars and pre-assigned 'live' coordinates. A 'Stochastic Update Loop' will run every 10 seconds, randomly incrementing or decrementing the occupancy status of specific cars to simulate live user reports. To mimic mobile network conditions, all data fetching will be wrapped in a 'Latency Wrapper' that injects a random delay of 500ms to 1500ms. User location will be emulated by following a hardcoded array of GPS coordinates that simulate a commuter moving through a station.
